subject: Audit period end-boundary and evidence timing

From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@acmehealth.com>

Cc: Sealaudit LLP <audit@sealaudit.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Jan 2027 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Clarification on SOC 2 Type II report coverage (end date inclusivity)

Hi Jasmine,

We're working through Acme Health's procurement checks and I have a couple quick questions about the SOC 2 Type II report you provided (covering the period ending Dec 31, 2026). The RFP asks for confirmation that the report's testing period includes controls exercised on the last day (Dec 31) and whether any control testing was limited to a point-in-time earlier in the month. Specifically: 

- Does "period ending Dec 31, 2026" mean tests were performed inclusive through 23:59 UTC on Dec 31 (or equivalent), or were there point-in-time testing cutoffs?
- If there are any known exceptions or controls that are only point-in-time, can you tell us which ones and whether those exceptions affect production access or audit-log availability?
- Acme also requested a bridge letter that extends coverage from Jan 1–Jan 15, 2027. Is Redwood able to provide a bridge letter affirming no changes to control design or operating effectiveness between Dec 31 and Jan 15? If so, what is the expected turnaround?

We need to respond to procurement by Jan 20. If it helps, the auditor (Sealaudit) is copied.

Thanks,
Laura Chen
Procurement Manager, Acme Health
laura.chen@acmehealth.com

[Attachment: RFP_Security_Questions.pdf (pdf)]

Hi Laura — thanks for the clear questions and for looping in Sealaudit. I can confirm a few things off the bat and will follow up with our compliance team for final wording. Quick answers: 

- Our published SOC 2 Type II report for period ending Dec 31, 2026 reflects testing that covers up to and including Dec 31; the intent is inclusive coverage across the full period. I'll confirm the exact timestamp convention (UTC vs. local) with compliance.
- I will check whether any controls were assessed only at a point-in-time (these are rare for our service controls) and, if so, provide a short list and whether they have any bearing on log access or production controls.
- We can typically provide a bridge letter for the requested window (Jan 1–Jan 15) that affirms no material changes to control design and no failed operating effectiveness items. I'll get an ETA from Marissa.

Marissa / Karthik — can you confirm the timestamp convention we use in our reports, whether any controls in the Dec 2026 report were point-in-time only, and whether compliance is comfortable issuing the bridge letter for Jan 1–15 (we may need a one-page signed letter).

I'll hold a short turnaround for Acme — they need a response by Jan 20.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Fwd: Clarification on SOC 2 Type II report coverage (need compliance wording)

Hi all — quick answers from Compliance / Audit ops: 

1) Timestamp convention: Our SOC 2 report uses inclusive period language. Testing coverage for period ending Dec 31, 2026 is inclusive through 23:59:59 UTC on 2026-12-31. We validate evidence through that timestamp when tests are sample-based or continuous.

2) Point-in-time controls: There are three administrative access reviews in the Dec 2026 report that were sampled as point-in-time checks (see index). Those checks do not affect production availability or audit-log retention; they are scoped to identity governance spot checks. We can provide the specific test IDs and sample artifacts on request.

3) Bridge letter: Compliance can issue a signed bridge letter covering Jan 1–Jan 15, 2027 stating there were no material changes to control design or failures of operating effectiveness during that window. Standard turnaround: 2 business days after we finalize wording and sign-off.

Attachments we can provide to Acme:
- Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2026.pdf (full report)
- Bridge_Letter_2026-12-31_to_2027-01-15.pdf (signed, once approved)
- Audit_Evidence_Index_2026.xlsx (index of artifacts and control test IDs)

Recommended redaction policy: remove user PII from sampled screenshots; otherwise provide original test logs. For remote access logs and token-level metrics we can share a read-only link to the logs console (see link).

Let me know if you want me to finalize the bridge wording; happy to draft and circulate for signatures.

Thanks — Marissa Cole
Head of Compliance, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
